graph.title: Space Rocket Ride

new_part_types.name: Plate 1x2 with two side handles (light grey)

notes: Element IDs on the inventory pages are 6-7 digit design/element codes; they were used as lego-<ID>. Several catalogue entries with the same ID have slightly different descriptive names, but the catalogue ID was used.

Ids b1..b154 follow build order; ids b36-b41, b101-b106, b114-b119, b128-b139 are intentionally absent because those pieces are generated by the roofarc, light and thruster repeats (2x yellow arch sub-assembly, 6x bracket+green+blue light, 2x cone thruster with two trans-red plates).

Each stud/anti-stud port is used by only one edge: parts that carry several neighbours (base plate, 1x10 brick, 4x6 hull plate, 1x6 bricks, corner bricks, etc.) have numbered stud/anti-stud ports in their new-type entries, and a different one is used per neighbour. Which stud number goes to which neighbour is arbitrary, the real positions can't be told apart in the small pictures. The 6 lights attach to b80:stud.11..16 via attach overrides.

Exact stud-to-stud positions are not always determinable from the small isometric pictures (e.g. which corner plate each yellow brick sits on, where the tiles in step 23 sit, how the front star panel of steps 16-22 mounts to the body, and the tail bracket/2x2 plate stack in steps 33-36); edges join the nearest plausible parent piece.
Step 3: the black 1x2 plate is assumed to sit under the dark-blue 2x3 plate at the base edge.

Crank mechanism (steps 9, 13-15): crank turns the white handle; tan pin + yellow bush carry the crank arm, liftarm links via blue pin; the 3-way brown connector with two white connectors rides on the tan pin and blue pin and carries the 3L axle that the rocket sits on. Pin/axle port assignments are a best interpretation.

The rocket's red 2x2 round plate with axle hole (b93, step 30) is assumed to be what receives the 3L axle in step 42; the nose cone (step 45) is assumed to push onto the black axle (b141) that goes through the nose Technic brick (step 39).
Bracket side holes are modelled as anti-stud-type ports ('side-hole') receiving round-plate studs for lights, the front-panel round plates and thruster cones.

Four 5-coin tiles: two are shown inside the red container; the other two are loose (cover shows them lying near the machine). They are connected by 'contact' edges to the base plate (resting on the surface) so they are not orphan nodes; they are not fastened to the model.
The minifigure is built on page 5 and shown beside the model on page 48; the cover shows it seated, so his legs are joined to the seat stud (b154 -> b110) as the final position.
Booklet contains a single model. Some steps (14, 15) re-use bush/axle pieces from the inventory with the second 4211573 and 4211622 assigned in order.
